approachQuestion.prompt: A scheduler assigns a nonnegative penalty to each slot. The charge of a nonempty contiguous interval is its smallest penalty. Return the sum of the charges over all such intervals, with no modulus. Penalties may repeat and are at most 1,000,000. Example: [2, 2, 1] returns 9: the three singleton charges sum to 5, the two length-two charges sum to 3, and the full interval contributes 1. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: For each position i, find the nearest strictly smaller penalty L on its left and the nearest smaller-or-equal penalty R on its right using ordered index stacks; use -1 and n for missing boundaries. Add penalty[i] × (i-L) × (R-i).
options.feedback: These boundaries assign each interval to its rightmost minimum. The independent left and right endpoint choices count every interval exactly once, including intervals containing equal minima.

options.text: Find the nearest strictly smaller penalty on both sides and add the same distance product for every position.
options.feedback: Equal minima both claim an interval. For [2, 2], each position claims the two-slot interval, producing 8 instead of 6.

options.text: Find the nearest smaller-or-equal penalty on both sides and add the same distance product for every position.
options.feedback: Equal values block one another on both sides. For [2, 2], neither position claims the two-slot interval, producing 4 instead of 6.

options.text: For every left endpoint extend a right endpoint, maintain the interval minimum, and add it to a total.
options.feedback: This is correct, including duplicates, but enumerates every interval and becomes quadratic. The ownership method avoids enumerating intervals.

feedback.reason: Assign each interval to exactly one minimum by using asymmetric boundaries for equal values.
details: Compute L by a left-to-right stack pass, removing top values greater than or equal to the current value. Compute R by a right-to-left pass, removing only strictly greater values. Save both boundary arrays and sum each value times its two endpoint-choice counts.
Use a strict boundary on one side and a non-strict boundary on the other so duplicate minima own each interval exactly once. Symmetric strictness would double-count or omit equal-minimum intervals.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For asymmetric-minimum-ownership, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the number of slots. Two boundary arrays and an index stack are allocated. Return a scalar; no input copy is made.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two boundary passes and one contribution sum are linear in n.
details: In each boundary pass an index is pushed once and popped once. Multiplying its left and right endpoint-choice counts aggregates many intervals with one word operation, so the final contribution scan is linear too. Boundary arrays and stack are O(n) helper storage. The potentially quadratic number of intervals does not require enumerating them.
